newsitem.title: USA: New FASB derivative rules seen delayed - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: New FASB derivative rules seen delayed - WSJ.

text.p: The U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board, which has been trying for a long time to introduce new derivatives accounting rules, plans to delay a June 30 deadline for the changes, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition on Friday.
FASB attributed the delay to corporate and congressional resistance to the proposed changes, the Journal said.
Dennis Beresford, chairman of FASB, was quoted as saying: "It sounds like it's highly unrealistic that we're going to make a June 30 deadline."
The Journal said FASB was aiming to have the new rules prepared by October but they could be delayed indefinitely.
FASB wants to have derivatives recorded on company balance sheets so investors can see their impact on results, the paper said.
